question: Which edit grouping and replay rules preserve user intent, and can competing history owners be removed?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles hard-cut comparison; two bounded independent native-consumer and authored/Yjs sidecars; source-first model diagnostics
trigger: User accepted the next ledger audit, history, after completing external-text. Assessment and local review recording only.
requirements: Assess all 10 history ledger units and materially different native, Plate, authored, collaboration, persistence and cancellation consumers without merging their independent feature reviews.
Undo and redo preserve local interaction intent across skipped/remote changes, domain effects, schema admission, exact selection/root identity and view retirement.
Supported replay composition must have coherent atomic stack and document semantics; unsupported composition must not silently produce incorrect history.
One grouping authority honors configured automatic delay while preserving long composition sessions and explicit semantic/path/root boundaries.
Atomic document/history load, authored compensation, and AI cancellation/replacement remain real adoption requirements.
Availability and mounted replay must avoid unnecessary full-stack work and preserve current pending-input, projected-selection and focus behavior.
evidenceReuse: First dedicated history review. Reaffirmed the transaction atomicity law, single canonical Yjs commit path and authored selective-reversal distinction against live source. The June OSS history research's skipped-overlap deletion invariant is present and passes in the current suite; old source names and performance figures were not reused as current proof. Two independent bounded sidecars supplied native-consumer source findings and 13 authored/Yjs test results; the lead checked decisive paths and ran its own distinct history, anchor, type and diagnostic proof. No fresh upstream discovery was needed.
summary: Pursue explicit replay on the existing history owner and one native grouping/mounted replay path. tx.history currently reads one published stack head and moves it after commit: two undos throw, undo/redo leaves text undone, and undo plus an edit loses normal edit history. React's separate 1000ms timer overrides configured delay in both directions. Ordinary availability reads materialize full branches. Proposed api.history replay remains provisional until atomic AI cancellation/replacement, outcomes, typed adoption and matched scale evidence are resolved; preserve transactional grouping/restore and authored compensation. Plate and Yjs already share one stack, so another backend abstraction is rejected.
alternatives: Keep/configure: retain canonical inverse changes, lazy skipped-change mapping, effects, bounded branches, validated persistence and root-aware selection. Configuration/caller discipline cannot repair demonstrated replay composition or the competing native timer.

Repair the current API: stage history heads, recovery and repeated/mixed replay in the transaction. This is the strongest alternative, especially for AI's real undo/discard/replace consumer, but needs an explicit mixed-edit and rollback law.

Move ownership/change API: pursue api.history.undo/redo as whole operations using the existing descriptor service and internal canonical update; preserve transactional edit policy and atomic document/history restore. Exact outcomes, availability and discard/cancellation adoption remain design questions.

Delete/merge/inline: remove the false transaction-replay promise only after atomic cancellation adoption, cut React's competing idle timer, consolidate duplicated mounted replay orchestration, and remove full-stack materialization from ordinary control reads. Retain native input/focus adapters and distribution facades for their independent jobs.
Add primitive: reject a generic history backend/session/manager or a Yjs-specific stack. Existing history, plugin API, canonical update and mounted view owners can carry the demonstrated work.

Replace architecture: universal document snapshots lose skipped edits/effects/identity; universal Yjs history burdens independent raw editing; merging authored selective compensation into local interaction stacks loses retention, attribution and dependency semantics.

Adoption counterfactual: compare removing AI historical branch surgery through existing preview/authored owners against full transaction-local history. Do not replace its atomic operation with separately visible undo and replacement updates.
proofLimits: 10 expected/10 reviewed/0 excluded/0 unreviewed or disposition-unresolved ledger units. Current history partition: 131 tests across five files pass; anchor history: 31 tests pass; history typecheck passes. Independent authored/Yjs sidecar: 13 selected tests across six files pass. Eight disposable diagnostics produce three passing controls/work-count observations and five expected composition/grouping failures. The availability diagnostic counts 20 transformations for 20 retained batches, not latency. Initial tx.string harness error is retained and excluded from product evidence. Toolbar metadata transfer/pending-input findings are source differences only, not browser-reproduced failures. No product edits, candidate runtime, matched performance comparison, browser/device run, declaration build, full gate or publication occurred. Proposed runtime target remains provisional and adoption is not complete. Autoreview was not run on next under branch policy.
